muhūrta
(‘a short unit of time’)
------------------------------------------
Measurement of time in certain units has been known to the Hindus since a long time. The word ‘muhūrta,’ meaning ‘a short time’, is one such unit known even to the वेदस् (vide Ṛgveda 3.35.5; 3.53.8 and Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.3.17).
However, in course of time, it became fixed as 1/30th part of a day of 24 hours and hence, of a duration of 48 minutes.
The 15 muhūrtas of a day (as different from those of the night) are sometimes given specific names such as brāhma-मुहूर्त, अभिजित्-मुहूर्त, vairāja-मुहूर्त and so on.
A proper मुहूर्त is one of the four elements—the other three being tithi, नक्षत्र and karaṇa—needed to be looked into for the success of an undertaking.
Muhūrtas considered auspicious for various acts, have been mentioned in the works on Hindu अस्त्रोलोग्य्. For instance: for purchasing merchandise, for the performance of auspicious acts, for wearing new garments for the first time, for उपनयन and मर्रिअगे and so on.
It is interesting to note that a work called Muhūrtamuktāvalī prescribes ‘auspicious’ time even for stealing!
However, certain sages have also declared that if there is purity of mind—as indicated by faith in God, honouring the holy ones and contentment—all the प्लनेत्स् will become favourable and hence there is no need to look for auspicious times (Matsyapurāṇa 243.25-27; Viṣṇu-dharmottarapurāṇa 2.163.32).
See also KĀLA.
